captions.detailed: A light grey bicycle front-end assembly consisting of a rigid fork and swept-back handlebars. The fork features a straight, cylindrical steerer tube branching down into a flat crown and two parallel, straight blade legs. A tall handlebar stem clamps onto the top of the steerer tube via a revolute joint, allowing angular adjustment, while the wide, swept-back handlebar curves backward and rotates within the stem clamp using another revolute joint.
captions.instruction: Generate a CAD model of a city bicycle fork and handlebar assembly in light grey. The assembly should feature a rigid fork with parallel blade legs, a tall height-adjustable stem, and a wide swept-back handlebar, incorporating revolute joints for both the stem-to-steerer clamp angle and the handlebar rotation inside the clamp.
captions.factory: Construct the fork by extruding a flat, rounded crown plate, then extruding a vertical cylindrical steerer tube upwards and two parallel cylindrical blade legs downwards. Create the stem as a vertical cylinder that terminates in an angled clamping collar. Form the swept-back handlebar by sweeping a circular profile along a curved path. Finally, assemble the parts using two revolute joints: one connecting the stem to the steerer tube, and another connecting the handlebar to the stem clamp.
